density.chosen_from: uniform over 1..4 per PLAN (the line-binding ceiling), from a stream seeded on (seed, 'density'); each line then draws its participation uniform over 1..1, and the end-rhyme pass binds free line ends on top (M-191)

end_rhyme.chosen_from: NOT A DRAW — each sung section's own `schemes[fn].rgs` re-realised at the line ends, so this consumes no seed entropy and the placement draw above is untouched. Three counts, never summed (doctrine 79): `added` groups emitted; `blocked` blocks whose ends the placement draw had already spent; `narrow` blocks whose lines cannot carry one more DISTINCT word.

execution.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

meter.chosen_from: 178 derived cycles (beats envelope [2, 12], slots envelope [5, 48]), measured BY DERIVATION ON THE DECLARED COORDINATE: 1 of 11 beats-per-line values, then 1 of 9 bars x subdivision factorisation(s) of 8 beats, then 1 of 1 groupings of 2. The line runs 8 beat(s) — at most the density band's ceiling, since a sung line carries at least one syllable a beat — and holds 16 slot(s), at least the band's floor. Both ends are the same calibrated band in different units; the pair share follows from how many ways each beat count factorises. Unit is notation, never enforced

narrative.chosen_from: uniform over the 1086 legal story line-ups of this shape (quality/narrative.py, M-121; the count is exact and the draw is entropy-last)

pattern.chosen_from: generated grammar: 22 cell types x 1..7 cells under the drawn total and declared brief, optional intro/outro/coda, roster 20 of 22 functions

placements.measure: uniform per MEMBER over the pool; per member and not per group because 8 of the 77 registered schemas anchor one member at each end of a word
placements.token_ceiling_from: the smaller of the floor's measured tokens-per-line floor 7.00 and this plan's own shortest line (12 syllable(s) after its pickup) less one for the last word — a plan asks for the n-th word only where BOTH the calibration and this meter say a line carries that many

relations.chosen_from: NOT DRAWN — the writer declared --relation and a declared coordinate is carried, never sampled over (M-55)

execution_limits.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution_limits.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

plan.writer_brief:
Write a song: 28 lines, 5 sections, in this order:
  [CHORUS — 5 lines — 20 bars of 2/4, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 5 lines — 20 bars of 2/4, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 7 lines — 28 bars of 2/4, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 7 lines — 28 bars of 2/4, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [BRIDGE — 4 lines — 16 bars of 2/4, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
Feel: 2/4 grouped 2.
Rhyme plan (line numbers over the whole song):
  lines 3.T5 & 5.T6 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1.T1 & 2.headrime & 4.T4 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11.head & 13.head & 16.headrime stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 12.T4 & 14.T7 & 17.T6 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 18.T5 & 20.head & 23.T3 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 19 & 21.T1 & 24 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 25 & 26.T2 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 27.T5 & 28.T2 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 3 & 5 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11 & 13 & 16 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 12 & 14 & 17 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 18 & 20 & 23 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
Story plan (one job per sung section; each enters from the section before it as stated):
  CHORUS1 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to
  CHORUS2 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — after CHORUS1
  VERSE1 lets the pressure in — set beside (connection unstated) CHORUS2
  VERSE2 cashes the standing pressure — after VERSE1
  BRIDGE1 flips the reading of everything before it — set beside (connection unstated) VERSE2
Every chorus after the first repeats the first chorus word for word, line for line.
Line 1 is the hook — make it the line someone leaves humming.
Where a binding sits (a bare line number is its end word, read as a rhyme span):
  T5: word 5, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T6: word 6, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T1: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  headrime: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T4: word 4, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  head: the first word, its first syllable — the head-rhyme / alliteration reading
  T7: word 7, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T3: word 3, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T2: word 2, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end

initial: Ring the bell that kept its scar; call us home

Let every bent note tell us where we are

Our hands lift brick dust out of the seam
The old bell keeps its red seam like a psalm

My father kept black filings in a bowl
Steam draws a white line down his leather neck
We wait until his scarred left hand lifts smoke
He says a flawless casting earns its name
Heat stains his cuffs; he will not strike the bell
I scratch the seam on glass beside his coat
We leave the split coal sacks out in the rain
The buyer wants a bell that keeps good time
Smoke drifts past his price list into the shade
Light from the furnace shows Eve's bitten lip
She sets the cracked old rim against her chest
Her palms hold the sound long past the gate
The crack lets out the note we kept inside
My father's rule still hangs above the room
A blue bruise blooms where Eve has held the bronze
He lays the worn stub of his chalk aside
The rust stays; now he asks her where to strike
